subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Clocks — Angles and Time Problems (Set W7)

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 5:00?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Hour hand at 5:00 = 5 × 30° = 150°. Minute hand at 12 = 0°. Angle = 150°. **Short Trick:** Each hour = 30°; at n o'clock, angle = n×30°. At 5:00, angle = 5×30 = 150°.

questions.stem: At 3:00, what is the angle between the hour and minute hands?
questions.explanation: C is correct. At 3:00, the hour hand is at 3×30° = 90° and the minute hand is at 0° (pointing to 12). Angle = 90°. At 3:00, the hands form a perfect right angle.

questions.stem: How many degrees does the minute hand of a clock sweep in one hour?
questions.explanation: C is correct. The minute hand completes one full revolution (360°) in 60 minutes = 1 hour. Speed of minute hand = 6° per minute. Hour hand moves only 30° per hour (0.5° per minute). So minute hand gains 5.5° per minute on the hour hand.

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands at 2:30?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Hour hand at 2:30: starts at 2×30°=60°, moves 30 min × 0.5°/min = 15° more → 75°. Minute hand at 30 min: 30×6° = 180°. Angle = |180° − 75°| = 105°. **Short Trick:** Angle = |30H − 5.5M| where H=hour, M=minutes. |30×2 − 5.5×30| = |60 − 165| = 105°.

questions.stem: At 6:30, what is the angle between the hour and minute hands?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Using |30H − 5.5M|: |30×6 − 5.5×30| = |180 − 165| = 15°. At 6:30 the minute hand is at 6 (180°) and the hour hand has moved halfway between 6 and 7 (195°). Angle = |195 − 180| = 15°.

questions.stem: At 4:20, what is the angle between the hour and minute hands?
questions.explanation: B is correct. |30×4 − 5.5×20| = |120 − 110| = 10°. Hour hand at 4:20 = 120 + 10 = 130°. Minute hand = 20×6 = 120°. Angle = 10°. Note: at 4:00 the angle is 120°; at 4:20 the minute hand has almost caught up to the hour hand, leaving only 10°.

questions.stem: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide (overlap) in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: B is correct. The hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours (not 12). Why? The minute hand laps the hour hand every 65 5/11 minutes, so 12 hours / (65 5/11 min) = 11 times. The hands coincide at 12:00:00, then ~1:05:27, ~2:10:54... but NOT at both 12:00 AM and 12:00 PM within the same 12-hour window.

questions.stem: At what time between 3 and 4 o'clock are the hour and minute hands together?
questions.explanation: B is correct. At 3:00, hour hand is 15 minute-marks ahead of minute hand. Minute hand gains 5.5 marks/minute. Time to close 15-mark gap: 15/5.5 = 30/11 = 2 8/11 minutes... wait, the gap at 3:00 is 15 mark-spaces. Actually: 15 / (5.5°/min) = 15 / (11/2) = 30/11 ≈ 2.7 min? That gives ~3:02.7, wrong. Correct: the gap is 90° = 15 minute positions, and minute hand gains 5.5°/min. 90/5.5 = 180/11 = 16 4/11 minutes. So hands meet at 16 4/11 minutes past 3.

questions.stem: A clock loses 5 minutes every hour. If it is set correctly at 10:00 AM, what time will it show when the actual time is 3:00 PM?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Actual elapsed time = 5 hours. Clock loses 5 min/hour → shows only 55 min for every actual 60 min. Clock time elapsed = 5 × (55/60) = 275/60 = 4 hours 35 minutes. Clock shows: 10:00 AM + 4h 35 min = 2:35 PM.

questions.stem: At what time between 7 and 8 o'clock do the clock hands first form a right angle (90°)?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Using formula: at m minutes past 7, angle = |30×7 − 5.5×m| = |210 − 5.5m|. For 90°: |210 − 5.5m| = 90. Case 1: 210 − 5.5m = 90 → m = 120/5.5 = 240/11 = 21 9/11 min (first right angle). Case 2: 5.5m − 210 = 90 → m = 300/5.5 = 54 6/11 min (second right angle). First occurrence = 21 9/11 min past 7.
